newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares jump 2.2 pct in late buying.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares jump 2.2 pct in late buying.

text.p: Istanbul shares leapt more than two percent in late buying on Thursday as liquidity rose at the same time as political tension eased, brokers said.
The IMKB National-100 which brushed a low of 1,425 in early trade, jumped to 1,459 at 1237 GMT in the last half hour of trade, up 2.24 percent from Wednesday.
"I think purchases are slowly picking up. Share deals made on loans which had stoppped for some time resumed. Political tension eased," said brokerage owner Mustafa Yilmaz.

Deputy prime minister Tansu Ciller said on Thursday her conservative True Path Party (DYP) would not abandon its Islamist coalition partners despite a row with the military and the resignation of two DYP ministers over the rise of Islamist activity.
"The DYP is not going to hide behind anyone and take part in action to topple the government," Ciller told a party meeting.
Brokers who await initial resistance at the index's 1,470 level, said selective purchases were based on good first quarter results of some companies.
